searchText: The PR with the executable beacon chain spec is opened, everybody is encouraged to look, comment, ask questions, discuss and so forth. Executable beacon chain is Ethereum Mainnet with PoS consensus, the main change that is coming within the Merge https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/pull/2229 <vbuterin> Here <vbuterin> Here's my attempt at an ultra-minimal merge spec: https://notes.ethereum.org/m9IX3OkkTveXCCOSzGkUiw I think fears about validators outsourcing to external block producers are extremely overblown. right now eth1vote isn't *that* important so I can see people doing that, but once the danger of outsourcing for actual block generation/verification is clearly communicated, there's no way people that locked a fortune to stake early (enthusiasts) are going to risk the security of the chain just to keep using that raspberry pi. in other words this would temporarily reduce the security to a honest majority assumption, which I think is guaranteed this early in eth staking what is TRANSITION_TOTAL_DIFFICULTY? a new constant? <vbuterin> yeah <vbuterin> It's the total difficulty level at which the transition happens <vbuterin> It has to be a totdiff and not a block number because otherwise an attacker could quietly mine a chain whose difficulty drops very low, and get to the number first <dankrad> The ethpow node has accepted the beacon block. -> the application_block? <vbuterin> ah yes <dankrad> we can use the same "synchronization" mechanism for transitioning to the executable beacon chain, right? <vbuterin> what do you mean by "transitioning to the executable beacon chain"? <dankrad> just wondering — this feels more like an "emergency merge" spec <dankrad> I mean finding the transition block, which was one of the challenges in the past <dankrad> the last PoW block <vbuterin> Doesn't the proposal address the problem of picking an end to the PoW chain as is? <dankrad> yes. Sorry, my bad. What I mean is use the mechanism you suggest in the quick merge for the executable beacon chain <vbuterin> yeah I don't understand what you mean by executable beacon chain then <vbuterin> The mechanism I suggest already gives you a beacon chain with application blocks being part of beacon blocks <dankrad> right, I mean this: https://ethresear.ch/t/executable-beacon-chain/8271 <vbuterin> ie. the chain-inside-a-chain is purely vestigial and can just be hard forked out <vbuterin> ah I see <vbuterin> migrating to that should be easy <vbuterin> At least relatively easy <vbuterin> Because once you have a block-inside-a-block the next step is to just remove the wrapper and have transactions-inside-a-block <vbuterin> There <vbuterin> There's a lot of prep work to be done, like turning the ethpow node into a simpler application state transition library, but that can be done between the hard forks with no consensus changes under this proposal, would beacon block proposers also be application block "miners" (and get both rewards)? <vbuterin> yes yes and note, in any pure proof-of-stake proposal that would be the case even if the application layer chain was not tightly coupled with the beacon chain cool, just wanted to confirm my understanding doesn't this concern apply to this proposal? https://ethresear.ch/t/executable-beacon-chain/8271/10 <dankrad> I think the proposal does not allow synchronous communication as it is <vbuterin> why not? <vbuterin> In the initial *implementation* it does not, because the *implementation* involves two nodes talking by RPC <dankrad> as in it's not specified <vbuterin> But that implementation can be swapped out with a synchronous implementation without a fork <vbuterin> And then a subsequent hard fork can add synchronous communication <dankrad> yeah I understand <dankrad> what I mean is your comment above was critical of requiring synchronous comms between beacon chain and eth1 execution because that requires keeping this structure forever <vbuterin> Ah, you're just saying "if we did this and then all retired 1 day later eth2 would not count as 'finished'"? <dankrad> no that's not what I'm saying. I was just replying to seishun <vbuterin> ah I see (re @ef_general_chat_bridge_bot: <seishun> doesn't this concern apply to this proposal? https://ethresear.ch/t/executable-beacon-chain/8271/10) <vbuterin> ah I see <dankrad> So even if executable data is directly inside beacon blocks I’d be inclined to favor keeping the communication between the executable data and the beacon chain logic fully asynchronous. your comment from back then <vbuterin> ah <vbuterin> ok <dankrad> which is probably sensible IMO as it allows us factoring it back out as a shard <vbuterin> And this proposal is 100% forward-compatible with both keeping the application block in the beacon chain _and_ making it a shard <dankrad> yup <dannyryan> yah, that is definitely a design goal <dannyryan> keeping the syncronous dependency minimal <dankrad> I think we can allow synchronous beacon chain -> eth1 <dankrad> just not the other way <dannyryan> because eth1 would be staggered after the beacon block from that slot <dannyryan> if it were a shard <vbuterin> hmm, by default I'd prefer not allowing synchronous anything just because that's forward compatible with more things <dankrad> even a shard always knows the latest beacon block root, so what's the harm in that? <dannyryan> in current spec, we only pass a few things from the beacon chain and it’s not the results of the execution. it’s things we can get at the immediate start of beacon execution e.g. pass the randao mix <dannyryan> e.g. the previous slot post beacon state root (current slot pre_state_root) <dannyryan> this looks like an optimal beacon/shard relationship <dannyryan> and keeps open the case where shard sees a beacon skip slot <dankrad> yes previous slot is still synchronous in my interpretation <dankrad> asynchronous is if you cannot guarantee a number of slots <dannyryan> ah, based on your delayed execution slot <dannyryan> ? (re @dankrad: asynchronous is if you cannot guarantee a number of slots) <dankrad> no, just generally synchronous = bounded delay asynchronous = unbounded delay is that not the definition? <dannyryan> that’s fine, you’d still get a pre-beacon-state root <dannyryan> because of skip slot processing <dannyryan> a shard has some beacon reference from the start of the current slot <dannyryan> which could be any numberof beacon skip slots

excerpts.author: 0xsadcat
excerpts.content: I think fears about validators outsourcing to external block producers are extremely overblown. right now eth1vote isn't *that* important so I can see people doing that, but once the danger of outsourcing for actual block generation/verification is clearly communicated, there's no way people that locked a fortune to stake early (enthusiasts) are going to risk the security of the chain just to keep using that raspberry pi. in other words this would temporarily reduce the security to a honest majority assumption, which I think is guaranteed this early in eth staking
